chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwaid, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, peace be upon them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said in his sermon:

"Shall I not inform you about the best virtues of this world and the hereafter? To forgive one who wronged you, to reconnect with one who severed ties with you, to show benevolence toward one who harmed you, and to give to one who deprived you.
And in mutual hatred lies the remover -- I do not mean the remover of hair, but the remover of faith."

key_terms.التباغض: Mutual hatred, reciprocal enmity between people
key_terms.الحالقة: The remover/destroyer -- a metaphor comparing hatred's effect on faith to a razor shaving hair
key_terms.العفو: Forgiveness, pardoning wrongs done to oneself

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say are the best virtues in this world and the hereafter?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) addresses his community in a sermon, listing five supreme virtues that benefit one both in this life and the hereafter: forgiveness, reconciliation, kindness to adversaries, generosity to the undeserving, and avoidance of mutual hatred. He then warns that mutual enmity is 'the remover' -- not of hair but of faith itself, using a vivid metaphor his audience would have immediately understood from the practice of head-shaving.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration
